candidate.answerReason: Under the recorded standard interpretation of uniform sampling by area, the favorable points form the disk of half the original radius. Its area is one fourth of the original area.

methods.label: Find the favorable disk
methods.explanation:
Interpret “at random” in the usual sense that equal areas are equally likely. Let the circular region have center \(O\) and radius \(R>0\), and let \(d=OP\) be the chosen point's distance from the center.

The distance from \(P\) to the boundary is \(R-d\). To see why, for any boundary point \(Q\), the shortest-path property gives
\[
OP+PQ\ge OQ=R,
\]
so \(PQ\ge R-d\). For \(P\ne O\), equality occurs along the radius extending from \(O\) through \(P\). At \(P=O\), every boundary point is distance \(R\), so the same formula holds.

Therefore the point is closer to the center exactly when
\[
d<R-d,\qquad\text{or}\qquad d<\frac R2.
\]
These points form the interior of a concentric circle of radius \(R/2\). Points on that circle are equally close to the center and boundary, so they are excluded; the circle itself has no area. The probability is consequently
\[
\frac{\pi(R/2)^2}{\pi R^2}=\frac14.
\]
The answer is \(\frac14\), choice A.
